subject: Session scoping, output custody, and regional export exemptions
messages:
From: Claire Summers <claire@novalabs.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@novalabs.com
Date: 2026-10-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Session scoping / DPA questions

Hi Karthik and Jordan,

Thanks for the call this morning — quick follow up from Nova legal/procurement. Attached is our redline (DPA_Nova_v1.pdf) and a small matrix that maps our different integration patterns to data flows (session-scoping-matrix.xlsx). Two asks we need explicit confirmation on before we move to procurement review: 

1) No-training commitment: we need an explicit clause that customer interactions (both prompts and associated chat responses) will not be used to improve or train any Redwood models unless we opt in via a separate agreement.

2) Output/Prompt custody: we need language confirming that Nova owns outputs and that prompt content will be treated as Nova data — we want to ensure there is no downstream use beyond troubleshooting unless expressly permitted.

3) Regional export exemptions: several of our EU customers require that EU-resident data never leaves the EU for model-improvement processing. We understand Redwood has hosted, dedicated, and private options — can you confirm the operational path for each (i.e., hosted with SCCs + onshore routing; Dedicated with reserved EU capacity; Private with on-prem/VPC)? We also need to understand how subprocessors factor into the EU-only requirement.

Can you confirm an evidence/timeline we can show procurement? We'd like to close this DPA + SOW by end of October.

Best,
Claire
Claire Summers
Legal Ops | Nova Labs

Attachments: DPA_Nova_v1.pdf (28KB), session-scoping-matrix.xlsx (12KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Claire Summers <claire@novalabs.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-14T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Session scoping / DPA questions

Claire — thanks for the clear notes and the attachments. Below is a concise operational position and proposed next steps so procurement has something concrete. Let me know if you want this reflected in the redline.

Summary position (short):
- No-training: Redwood will agree to a no-training commitment for Nova data by default. We will not use prompts or responses to update model weights or training corpora unless Nova signs an explicit opt-in amendment. We can add the specific "no-model-improvement" clause you requested.
- Output & prompt custody: Nova retains ownership of prompts and generated outputs. Redwood will process and store content as necessary to serve requests and for short-term troubleshooting/telemetry, but we will not assert IP rights over customer outputs.
- EU regional handling: three options we can offer and operational guarantees:
  * Hosted: EU-region model serving with SCCs for transfers + geo-routing. Telemetry used for system health will be aggregated and pseudonymized; we can suppress capture for flagged sessions.
  * Dedicated: dedicated GPU pools in EU (reserved capacity) — no cross-border export for the reserved workload unless explicitly enabled.
  * Private (VPC/on-prem): full EU residency; minimal subprocessors (list provided) and KMS/HSM integration available.
- Subprocessors: we will provide our current subprocessor register and agree to notify for any changes. For Nova's EU-only requirement we can commit to a subprocessor gating workflow: either (a) restrict to subprocessors with EU presence, or (b) offer Private deployment to avoid cross-border subprocessors.

Operational evidence & timeline:
- We will deliver a one-page "implementation evidence" PDF showing region routing, KMS residency, and subprocessor list by EOD 2026-10-18.
- If you need SOC2/SecOps artifacts, we can deliver a redacted pack within 5 business days after LOI.
- Proposed DPA redline changes: add no-model-improvement clause; add explicit ownership sentence for outputs; add subprocessor gating appendix. I can send a legal-approved markup for your counsel to review by 2026-10-16.

Next steps:
1) Confirm you want the no-training language as written (I will attach our standard wording).
2) Let us know if Dedicated EU-only or Private is required for signoff — that will drive procurement/costing.
3) We will prepare the evidence pack and a short mutual action plan for procurement.

Jordan/Hannah: looping you for technical confirmation on the suppression/tagging approach and subprocessor gating workflow.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Quoted attachment references preserved.

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: Claire Summers <claire@novalabs.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-15T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Session scoping / DPA questions

Claire — quick technical notes to back up Karthik's email: 

1) Suppression & tagging: we have an SDK flag and API header (X-Redwood-Persist: false) customers can set to mark sessions as non-capture. For hosted flows where the header isn't set by the client, we can provide a session-scoping proxy that strips telemetry before it's recorded. This is how we ensure ephemeral sessions remain non-consumptive for model improvement.

2) KV/cache & troubleshooting: short-term KV cache (ephemeral by default) is kept for latency; we can configure TTLs and a retention policy per Nova SOW. For troubleshooting we retain minimally sufficient logs and can provide redacted samples in evidence packs.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: our current subprocessor list includes a few EU-hosted partners and one US-based monitoring vendor. For EU-only workloads we recommend either (a) Dedicated EU capacity, or (b) Private deployment with your VPC so no US subprocessors are in the path. If you choose Dedicated we can implement onshore-only routing and block cross-border export at the routing layer.

4) Evidence pack: we'll include an export diagram showing routing + SCCs (if Hosted), a copy of the subprocessor register, and the sample KMS integration steps. That should be sufficient for procurement and legal to evaluate compliance.

If Nova can confirm the preferred deployment model (Hosted EU, Dedicated EU, or Private) I can put together a short ops runbook for their integration team. Happy to do a 30-min technical call if helpful.

— Jordan
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Claire Summers <claire@novalabs.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@novalabs.com
Date: 2026-10-15T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Session scoping / DPA questions

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail procurement wanted. A few quick confirmations and a small requested tweak to the DPA redline: 

* Nova accepts the standard no-model-improvement clause but would like one sentence added that "customer data will not be used to fine-tune or update model parameters, embeddings, or training datasets now or in the future without explicit written consent."
* For Hosted: we will accept Hosted EU-region with SCCs if you provide an implementation evidence PDF and confirm the telemetry suppression proxy will be available at cutover.
* For subprocessors: procurement would like the current register and a 30-day notice window for any new subprocessors. Please include that in the subprocessor appendix.

Request: Can you send the DPA markup with the added sentence and the one-page implementation evidence by EOD Monday (2026-10-18)? If so, procurement will initiate the final review and DocuSign path.
